item.title: U.S.-Iran war appears to pause as Trump gives "diplomacy a chance"
item.description: The U.S. and Iran hold fire amid work on a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but the Trump administration says a military buildup continues.

item.title: Latest details on deadly Seattle food festival shooting as police search for second suspect
item.description: At least three people are dead, and four are injured after a Sunday night shooting at a food festival near the Seattle Space Needle, police said. CBS News' Bradley Blackburn has the latest.

item.title: 3 killed, 4 wounded in shooting near Seattle's Space Needle, authorities say
item.description: Three people were killed and four others wounded in a shooting during a food festival at the Seattle Center near the Space Needle, police said. A suspect was in custody and another was being sought, they said.

item.title: Video appears to show person kicking sea lion: "Disgusting act"
item.description: The video appears to show a person throwing kicks at the sea lion at La Jolla Cove as at least one other person can be heard laughing in the background.

item.title: Massive wildfires in France, Spain being fought ahead of forecast heat wave
item.description: Hundreds of thousands remained evacuated as huge wildfires burned in France and Spain. A race against time saw firefighters trying to make progress before a forecast surge in temperatures.

item.title: GOP spent years targeting progressive dark money. That could boomerang on Trump.
item.description: The Trump-linked group Freedom 250 staged America's birthday with tens of millions that it is not required to disclose.

item.title: Cyclospora boosts fears that deadlier foodborne outbreaks are ahead
item.description: Food safety experts say cuts to the public health system hobbled the response — and that the next outbreak could be much worse.

item.title: U.S. halts strikes on Iran for second night as talks move in positive direction
item.description: Talks between Oman and Iran on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and their respective territorial waterways have made progress, two sources told CBS News.

item.title: Pentagon lists 4 killed in Iran war under "Overseas Operations Casualties"
item.description: Four U.S. service members who were listed in a Pentagon casualties database as having died during the Iran war are now listed as "Overseas Operations Casualties."

item.title: Colorado River reservoirs hit record lows as government threatens major cuts
item.description: It's a moment of reckoning in the drought-stricken West as seven states can't agree on how to share the rapidly shrinking water supply.

item.title: Oil prices top of mind at the Calgary Stampede rodeo
item.description: The Calgary Stampede is the largest outdoor rodeo in the world. And with Alberta holding the fourth-largest proven oil reserve in the world, high oil prices are playing a part in the show. Ian Lee reports.

item.title: New aerial video of deadly subway surfing trend released by NYPD
item.description: This weekend, New York City police released new video of a deadly trend known as subway surfing. Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: States relying on Colorado River water face major cuts as reservoir levels fall to all-time lows
item.description: The Colorado River, a lifeline for the American West, is now a line in the sand dividing seven states that can't agree how to share the shrinking water supply. After years of failed talks, the federal government is now poised to impose sweeping cuts. Jonathan Vigliotti reports.

item.title: Berlin Pride attacker served time for trying to join ISIS, officials say
item.description: The suspect, identified as 21-year-old Abdul Ballout, was killed in a confrontation with police in a suburb of Berlin, police said.

item.title: 2-day pause in Iran strikes linked to progress in diplomatic talks, sources say
item.description: The current two-day pause in fighting between the U.S. and Iran comes after nearly two straight weeks of intense fighting and is directly linked to progress in diplomatic efforts, sources confirm to CBS News. At the same time, there are growing concerns that the U.S. is running low on crucial munitions. Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: Bad numbers for Trump on economy, Iran, in latest CBS News poll
item.description: A new CBS News poll found that 65% of Americans disapprove of how President Trump is handling the economy, 71% disapprove of his handling of inflation and 63% think the war in Iran is going badly for the United States. Olivia Gazis reports.

item.title: What to know about the Berlin Pride attack and the suspect killed by police
item.description: One woman was killed and at least 29 others were hurt when prosecutors say 21-year-old Abdul Ballout allegedly drove a rented van into crowds celebrating Berlin Pride on Saturday. On Sunday, police shot and killed Ballout after they say he charged at officers with a bladed weapon. Imtiaz Tyab reports.

item.title: Carlos Beltrán, Andruw Jones and Jeff Kent inducted into Baseball Hall of Fame
item.description: Center fielders Carlos Beltrán and Andruw Jones and second baseman Jeff Kent were inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame on Sunday.

item.title: Why the COVID vaccine isn't part of an injury compensation court
item.description: A federal court compensates people who say they were injured by vaccines. Here is why the COVID vaccines are not currently part of it.

item.title: 7/26/2026: Vaccine Court; Chess Boxing; Amy Sherald
item.description: First, inside the U.S. vaccine court. Then, a look at chess boxing: a sport where brain meets brawn. And, Amy Sherald: The 60 Minutes Interview.

item.title: 7/26: CBS Weekend News
item.description: What to know about the Berlin Pride attack and the suspect killed by police; Bad numbers for Trump on economy, Iran, in latest CBS News poll.

item.title: U.S. appeals court upholds ruling blocking Trump's order on mail-in voting
item.description: A federal appeals court has upheld a judge's ruling that halted President Trump's efforts to create a federal voter list and limit who can receive a mail ballot.

item.title: Home, not alone: Helping aging seniors in rural America
item.description: Health risks associated with loneliness and social isolation are more common among the aging population of rural America. In North Dakota, the program Aging in Community aims to build connections among neighbors to help isolated rural seniors.

item.title: 7/26: Face The Nation
item.description: This week on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," Sens. Bernie Sanders and John Kennedy join, along with U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz and former FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb. Plus, CBS News' Anthony Salvanto has the latest poll results.

item.title: How Trump admin cuts have compromised food safety
item.description: Since May, more than 11,000 cases of illness caused by the parasite cyclospora have been reported in 41 states. This comes after the Trump administration drastically cut FDA and CDC staff, prompting one expert to call this summer's outbreaks "a national wake-up call."

item.title: ICE to target Haitians as Temporary Protected Status is set to end, sources say
item.description: The plans include arresting migrants in Ohio and quickly putting them on deportation flights to crisis-stricken Haiti, the internal documents indicate.

item.title: CBS News poll finds many changing their eating habits amid cyclospora outbreak
item.description: Nearly as many Americans are following news about the cyclospora parasite as they are the conflict with Iran.

item.title: Russian Soyuz brings three home after 8 months at space station
item.description: The Soyuz MS-28 landing in Kazakhstan brought a 241-day stay in space to a successful conclusion.

item.title: "48 Hours" show schedule
item.description: True crime. Real justice. To miss it would be a crime.

item.title: Pentagon website "anomalies" that removed names of 4 killed in Iran war remain
item.description: The Pentagon website, which was last updated on July 22, still showed only 14 killed in the conflict as of Friday.
